description: Enumerate natural {1/(4π), b₁=8, g=4, P=2} combinations landing on the per-loop measure 1/(8π); test whether the coefficient is naive-mode-countable (forced) or requires the #3911 theta-factor (not separable).

data.verdict: The α_EM per-loop measure 1/(8π) is reproduced by 6 distinct natural combinations of the settled data {1/(4π), b₁=8, g=4, P=2} (hk /count P=2; hk /count b1/g=2; hk/2 /count 1; hk/2 *count 1; 2hk /count g=4; 2hk /count b1/P=4). Since MORE THAN ONE lands on 1/(8π) and no forcing principle singles one out, the coefficient is NOT naive-mode-countable: the reciprocal-form and the `8π = 2·4π` multiplicity do NOT separate from the magnitude, so `8π` cannot be honestly derived by arithmetic bookkeeping — it must come from the genuine polarized-Jacobian genus-4 theta-factor computation (#3911). This is the anti-laundering result: it forecloses reverse-engineering 8π from a hand-picked combination. The count b₁=8 and π-power 1/(4π) are settled; the JOINT coefficient is one object with the magnitude leg, not a separable arithmetic piece. No fit; no c_k; nothing wired; no tier change.
